headline: Funding flows. Satellites multiply. Defense budgets swell.
deck: This week saw significant funding rounds and strategic partnerships in the space sector.

stories.head: Apex's valuation skyrockets to $2.3 billion
stories.body: Apex has raised $200 million, pushing its valuation to $2.3 billion. This surge indicates a strong demand for satellite technology, particularly in a market where productized satellite buses are gaining traction. Investors seem to believe that the satellite game is not just about the number of launches but the efficiency of the platforms.
stories.soWhat: Apex's rise suggests that investors are betting heavily on the commodification of satellite technology, which could make the market even more competitive.

stories.head: Anduril and L3Harris unite for SDA bid
stories.body: Anduril and L3Harris have partnered to pursue a tactical Space Development Agency (SDA) constellation bid. This collaboration reflects a growing trend where defense contractors are pooling resources to tackle complex satellite challenges, especially in a landscape where the stakes are high, and budgets are expanding.
stories.soWhat: When big players team up, it’s often a sign that the competition is heating up—and that might mean more lucrative contracts down the line.

stories.head: Exploration Company inches closer to Nyx launch
stories.body: The Exploration Company has successfully completed a drop test of its Nyx capsule, with plans for a test flight in 2028. This is a small but meaningful step towards proving that their ambitious lunar plans are more than just PowerPoint slides. As companies race to establish a presence on the Moon, every test counts.
stories.soWhat: If they can keep this momentum, they might just beat the rush to the Moon—assuming the Moon doesn't get too crowded first.

watchlist.title: Watch for Apex's next moves post-funding
watchlist.body: With a valuation of $2.3 billion, Apex's next strategic decisions could set the tone for satellite manufacturing in the coming months.

watchlist.title: Potential IPOs on the horizon
watchlist.body: As the defense-tech IPO window opens, expect more companies to explore public offerings, which could reshape funding dynamics in space.

watchlist.title: NASA's Artemis 2 crew returns
watchlist.body: The successful orbit of the Moon by Artemis 2 could reignite interest in lunar missions and related technologies next week.

watchlist.title: Hypersonic testing delays continue
watchlist.body: The ongoing delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle testing may prompt defense contractors to pivot their focus towards more reliable technologies.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
